input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Sec 2.1 imposes a three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely in the rule's walk-away territory (multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right) and well short of the fallback (single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty). It also conflicts with our termination-for-convenience right in Sec 9.4, Sec 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and Sec 7.1's bar on undisclosed minimum-use charges. We propose the preferred position — no minimum commitment, payment for Services ordered/used — which is consistent with the rest of the bargain, with the 12-month reducible commitment plus true-up offered as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2m take-or-pay minimum in Sec 2.1; Fees payable only for Services ordered and used.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept multi-year take-or-pay commitments, so we have replaced the three-year USD 2,000,000 minimum with payment for Services actually ordered and used - this also aligns Sec 2.1 with our termination-for-convenience right in Sec 9.4 and the no-minimum-volume acknowledgement in Sec 12.3. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or volume commitment. Customer pays only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form and, where an Order Form provides usage-based pricing, actually used.
